newsitem.title: USA: NFL-MORA RESIGNS AS COACH OF NEW ORLEANS SAINTS.
newsitem.headline: NFL-MORA RESIGNS AS COACH OF NEW ORLEANS SAINTS.

text.p: Jim Mora has resigned in his 11th season as head coach of the New Orleans Saints, the National Football League team said Monday.
Saints owner Tom Benson said a search for a new head coach will begin immediately. The 2-6 Saints have a bye next week before facing the San Francisco 49ers on November 3.
Mora, who had the longest current tenure as coach of the same team in the NFL, quit one day after he ripped into his team following a 19-7 loss at Carolina.

"We got our butts kicked, we couldn't do anything," said Mora after Sunday's loss. "It was an awful performance. I am embarrassed and ashamed of our team. We could not stop them and we could not move the ball.
"They blocked better, they were tougher and they were coached better."
After losing their first five games, New Orleans recorded back-to-back wins over Jacksonville and Chicago. But the Saints managed only 10 first downs in Sunday's loss to the Panthers.

Mora, 61, resigned a few hours after the Cincinnati Bengals made the first head coaching change in the NFL this season. The Bengals fired David Shula and named offensive coordinator Bruce Coslet as his replacement.
Buffalo Bills coach Marv Levy becomes the active leader in coaching tenure with the same team. Levy started coaching the Bills in the second half of the 1986 season.

Mora, whose overall record with the Saints, including playoffs, was 93-78, was believed to be on the way out last year after New Orleans opened the season with five losses. But the Saints won seven of their last 11 to finish 7-9.
